items.problem: Data-bound NavigationView master/detail: selecting scenarios 2-9 highlights the item but never switches the content Frame, so 8/9 scenarios are unreachable at runtime.
items.evidence: migration-score.json (8 fail); session-log NavView_ItemInvoked copied from skill snippet reads `args.InvokedItemContainer?.DataContext is Scenario s` (session-log turns ~3617-3624).
items.root_cause: The snippet resolves the invoked data item via the item CONTAINER's DataContext. Under a NavigationView.MenuItemTemplate the container's DataContext is not reliably the bound data object, so `is Scenario s` is false and Navigate never runs. Microsoft docs state NavigationViewItemInvokedEventArgs.InvokedItem IS the invoked data item — the snippet contradicts its own surrounding prose (which correctly says 'the invoked item is the bound data item').
items.proposed_fix: Replace the buggy MenuItemsSource handler body with the direct, documented form: `private void NavView_ItemInvoked(NavigationView sender, NavigationViewItemInvokedEventArgs args) { if (args.InvokedItem is Scenario s) ScenarioFrame.Navigate(s.ClassType); }` and delete the confusing empty first if-block. Keep the explicit initial navigation on Loaded.
items.generalizes: Every UWP SDK-sample and most master/detail apps migrate their scenario/section list to a data-bound NavigationView (MenuItemsSource + MenuItemTemplate). Any migration that copies this snippet inherits the dead-scenario bug. Using args.InvokedItem is the correct, framework-guaranteed route for all data-bound NavigationViews.
